identification.name: Synfoam SW-9 Syntactic Foam
identification.common_form_notes: Supplied as fully-cured solid blocks (6" × 12" × 24") rather than sheet/plate stock in the conventional sense — machined by the end user into custom shapes and sizes. "Plate" is the closest available form option; treat it as an approximation for a solid cast block.
identification.notes: A particle-reinforced composite: hollow glass microspheres embedded in a resin (typically epoxy) matrix, engineered specifically for buoyancy under sustained hydrostatic pressure — unlike closed-cell foams, the rigid glass microspheres resist crushing/collapse at depth, so buoyancy is retained rather than lost under pressure. Density and compressive strength are cross-validated by two independent sources (MatWeb and the manufacturer's own site) agreeing closely: the manufacturer specifies SW-9 as a 9 ± 1 lb/ft³ grade (nominal 0.144 g/cm³, tolerance range 0.128–0.160 g/cm³ — stored value uses this manufacturer nominal rather than MatWeb's slightly different unlabeled range of 0.112–0.176 g/cc) with compressive strength of 300 psi = 2.07 MPa, an exact match to MatWeb's independently-stated 2.07 MPa. Depth rating (100 m) and service pressure (145 psi) also match exactly between both sources, and are internally self-consistent: 100 m of seawater produces almost exactly 145 psi of hydrostatic pressure (ρgh). Water absorption is specified by the manufacturer as <5% (24 hours at depth) — a maximum spec, not currently tracked as a property in this database. The manufacturer's full "Standard Properties" table resolves the earlier ambiguity about the product line's depth range definitively: SW-5 (50 m) / SW-9 (100 m) / SW-12 (150 m) / SW-15 (200 m) / SW-18 (500 m) — confirming SW-9 specifically is a shallow-water grade, while general marketing language describing the line as good to "1,000 m" refers to the family's higher-density end (SW-18 reaches 500 m per the spec table; the 1,000 m figure may describe a newer/different grade or be a rounded marketing claim, not literally SW-18's spec). This matches realistic capstone AUV/ROV pool/shallow-water testing depths rather than full-ocean-depth applications. DATA GAP: no modulus, tensile strength, Poisson's ratio, or thermal properties are available from either source — a genuine limitation, not an oversight. Compressive strength (2.07 MPa) is very low in absolute terms compared to structural materials elsewhere in this database — appropriate, since this material's design role is buoyancy, not load-bearing strength. Electrical conductivity is nominally 0% IACS (International Annealed Copper Standard) — the glass-microsphere/epoxy matrix is an electrical insulator, not a specific sourced measurement.

typical_usage: Buoyancy modules and flotation for underwater vehicles (AUVs — autonomous underwater vehicles — and ROVs — remotely operated vehicles), instrumentation housings, and subsea equipment needing reliable, depth-stable buoyancy without the water absorption and pressure-collapse issues of conventional closed-cell foams. Select a grade primarily by required depth/pressure rating and target buoyancy (density) — this SW-9 (shallow-water) grade suits pool/lake/shallow-ocean testing; denser grades in the same product family extend to much greater depths at the cost of reduced buoyancy.
